report.summary: Chunk 3 of worktree.py: defines inode identity helpers, reparse-safe removal primitives, chain_between, and _remove_tree_no_follow with invariant documentation.
risks: _remove_tree_no_follow | high | The invariant claims exactly three verification sites but the code for those sites is not in this chunk. | Check the full function body for the scan, unlink, and rmdir drain sites.
_chain_between | medium | Uses _key comparison; if _key raises or is inconsistent, the loop may behave unexpectedly. | Verify _key implementation.

_unlink_reparse_point | medium | Falls back to unlink after rmdir; if path is a directory symlink on some platforms, rmdir may succeed, but if it fails on a file symlink, unlink is tried; order may not be correct for all platforms. | Confirm platform behavior.
_force_unlink | low | Calls _clear_readonly only on PermissionError; other OSError types are unhandled. | Decide if other errors should be caught.

handoff.purpose: Define inode-based identity, reparse-safe removal helpers, chain_between, and start of _remove_tree_no_follow with invariant.

symbols.name: _key
symbols.note: Returns (st_dev, st_ino) tuple from lstat, or None on error. Docstring explains inode semantics and 0-value handling.

symbols.name: _lexists
symbols.note: Returns True if os.lstat succeeds, False on OSError/ValueError.

symbols.name: _clear_readonly
symbols.note: Tries to clear readonly bit via os.chmod; best-effort, passes on OSError.

symbols.name: _unlink_reparse_point
symbols.note: Removes the link itself: tries rmdir then unlink, with readonly fallback.

symbols.name: _force_unlink
symbols.note: Unlinks a file; on PermissionError clears readonly and retries.

symbols.name: _force_rmdir
symbols.note: Rmdirs a directory; on PermissionError clears readonly and retries.

symbols.name: _chain_between
symbols.note: Returns list of Path components from root to target, walking upward by _key. Raises ValueError if root not on target's path.

symbols.name: _remove_tree_no_follow
symbols.note: Recursively deletes root without traversing reparse points. Invariant documented but body not fully shown.

claims.text: a renamed directory keeps its record and a fresh object cannot be handed that record while the renamed one still holds it
claims.why: This claim about record-handing behavior is not verifiable from the code in this chunk.

claims.text: a fresh directory OR JUNCTION created at the vacated name gets a different ``st_ino``
claims.why: The function returns (st_dev, st_ino) from lstat, so a new directory/junction will have a different inode if the filesystem provides one.

claims.text: ``st_ino`` is 0 on filesystems that do not expose one (FAT, some network mounts). Callers must treat a zero ``st_ino`` as NO identity rather than as a comparable value
claims.why: The docstring states this; the code returns the raw inode value, so it can be 0. No handling of 0 is done here.

claims.text: see :meth:`GitWorktreeManager._refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved`, which is why that method also has a check that does not depend on inodes.
claims.why: Reference to a method not in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: ``os.chmod``, ``os.unlink`` and ``os.rmdir`` resolve their path ARGUMENT through a reparse point in any intermediate component, exactly as ``os.scandir`` does. (What they do NOT do is follow a reparse point that is the FINAL component -- rmdir removes the junction, unlink removes the link.)
claims.why: The comment describes behavior of these syscalls; the code uses them, so the claim is consistent with this chunk.

claims.text: none of them is safe on the strength of a check that happened earlier: every caller here re-verifies the whole chain immediately before calling them.
claims.why: The code for callers is not in this chunk; cannot verify re-verification.

claims.text: An earlier version believed ``os.scandir`` was the only follower, and the rmdir drain that belief licensed was measured deleting 3000 directories inside a stand-in primary checkout, 3/3, while reporting success.
claims.why: Historical claim; not verifiable from current code.

claims.text: EVERY path handed to a syscall that RESOLVES it -- ``os.scandir``, ``os.rmdir``, ``os.unlink``, ``os.chmod`` -- is re-classified with a FRESH ``lstat`` IMMEDIATELY beforehand, together with every component above it, up to and including ``guarded_ancestors``.
claims.why: The body of _remove_tree_no_follow is not fully shown; cannot verify that every syscall is preceded by a fresh lstat.

claims.text: There are exactly three such sites (the scan, the per-child unlink, the rmdir drain) and all three verify.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete; cannot verify the number or presence of verification sites.

claims.text: No path in this function is acted on twice on the strength of one check.
claims.why: Cannot verify without the full function body.

claims.text: Raises ``ValueError`` if ``root`` is not on ``target``'s path.
claims.why: The code explicitly raises ValueError when parent == current, indicating root not found on path.

observations.what: _key returns None on OSError/ValueError; callers must handle None.
_lexists returns False on OSError/ValueError; does not distinguish between 'does not exist' and other errors.
_chain_between uses _key for comparison; if _key returns None for any component, the while condition may fail or raise.
_remove_tree_no_follow docstring claims invariant but the body is incomplete in this chunk.
